findings.title: No-auth trust boundary
findings.summary: The ACT server mounts only cors(), express.static, express.json — zero authentication/authorization on any REST or Socket.io route. Anything that can reach the bound port can create/complete/validate tasks, register agents, and read the full ChronLog.

findings.title: QA synthesis = boundary marker, not full deliverable persistence
findings.summary: POST /api/tasks/:id/synthesis (kind=complete) only stamps metadata.synthesizedAt and logs a summary STRING; the assembled final deliverable is never persisted server-side. The done-marker half works; the deliverable-storage half does not.

findings.title: 95% validation gate is prompt-enforced server-side, code-backstopped orchestrator-side
findings.summary: POST /api/tasks/:id/validation-verdict trusts the caller's passed/score verbatim — there is NO server-side 95% threshold check; the e2e fixture posts passed:true score:95 with criteriaResults:[] directly. The 95% gate lives in the Assurance prompt. The orchestrator's parseValidationVerdict adds a CODE backstop (passThreshold=95 + FAIL-CLOSED on empty criteria, Fix 23), but the SERVER endpoint itself records whatever verdict it is handed.

findings.title: ACP-backed Tier-1 shim CLI path is unbootstrapped by the installer
findings.summary: REPLACES the inventory's false FT1-1. The shim (cmd/act-tier1-shim) execs exec.Command('act', ...) and relies on act-tier1-<role> symlinks on PATH, but install.sh creates ONLY an 'act-agent' symlink (and deliberately REMOVES any old 'act' symlink to avoid the nektos/act collision) and never creates the act-tier1-<role> symlinks at all. So after a standard install, ACP-backed Tier-1 agents cannot resolve either the 'act' binary name or their role shims — the whole shim CLI surface (status/log/validation/prompt-section/etc.) is dead. NOTE: prompt-section itself is NOT a dead path — cmd/root.go:689 handles it natively pre-cobra; the in-process Planner reaches it via the expand_prompt_section tool. The gap is install-time bootstrap of the ACP shim, not the section registry.
findings.evidence: act-agent/cmd/act-tier1-shim/main.go:134 (exec.Command 'act'); install.sh:46 (only act-agent symlink), install.sh:182-184 (removes old act symlink); grep 'act-tier1' install.sh returns nothing; native prompt-section route cmd/root.go:689,468

findings.summary: buildCommand routes antigravity/agy to antigravityCLIDefaults which spawns `node agy-acp.mjs`; app.go's switch, slash.go's validator, and config.validateAgent all accept them, and the tree builds clean. An agent reading the working tree sees a wired agy backend; a fresh clone of feat/remove-nomik HEAD does NOT have it.

findings.title: antigravity backend is Tier-1-only; the CLI advertises it for Tier 2 where it is rejected
findings.summary: `act-agent swarm set <role> antigravity` passes the CLI's VALID_BACKENDS check (act-cli.ts:552) and writes agents.<role>.backend='antigravity', but the Tier-2 path refuses it: runner.IsValidBackend accepts only act-agent/claude-code (swarm_roles.go:44-46) and act-runner.mjs runAgent has no antigravity branch (only claude-code vs act-agent). A user can configure a swarm backend that silently never starts. antigravity/agy is real only on the Tier-1 ACP path.

findings.title: act-cli --help command table omits `swarm` — doc/code drift
findings.summary: The help `commands` object in act-cli.ts (lines 1000-1023) lists ~20 entries but does NOT include `swarm`, even though `swarm` is a live dispatch branch (act-cli.ts:1281) and the documented CLI surface for Tier-2 backend selection. A user running help never sees swarm. The dispatch chain is the source of truth; the help table is stale relative to it.

findings.title: Runner TASK_TIMEOUT default (120s) can guillotine long swarm tasks
findings.summary: act-runner.mjs TASK_TIMEOUT defaults to 120000ms for a single agent invocation. Real implementation tasks routinely exceed 2 minutes; on timeout the subprocess is killed and reportComplete fires with success=false, sending the task back through retry. Config knob (TASK_TIMEOUT_MS) exists but the default is aggressive for the swarm's actual workload.
